chapter: Unit 14 Transportation in Plants and Circulation in Animals
text:
UNIT 14 TRANSPORTATION IN PLANTS AND CIRCULATION IN ANIMALS

DOUBLE CIRCULATION, BLOOD PRESSURE, AND BLOOD GROUPS (PAGE 204)

Human circulation is completely double: 1. Pulmonary circulation: deoxygenated blood pumped from right ventricle to lungs for oxygenation and returns to left atrium. 2. Systemic circulation: oxygenated blood pumped from left ventricle through aorta to systemic tissues and deoxygenated blood returns to right atrium via vena cavae. Pacemaker Sinoatrial (SA) node initiates myogenic electrical impulses. Blood pressure measured with sphygmomanometer: normal reading is 120/80 mmHg (systolic/diastolic). Karl Landsteiner discovered ABO blood groups determined by antigens A and B on erythrocytes and antibodies in plasma; Rh factor (+/-) determines Rh compatibility.
text_ta:
Unit 14 Transportation in Plants and Circulation in Animals

Double Circulation, Blood Pressure, and Blood Groups (பக்கம் 204)

இரட்டை ரத்த ஓட்டம், ரத்த அழுத்தம் மற்றும் ரத்த வகைகள்: நுரையீரல் சுற்றோட்டம் மற்றும் உடல் சுற்றோட்டம். சைனோ-ஆரிக்குலார் (SA) கணு இதயத்தின் துடிப்பை உருவாக்கும் பேஸ்மேக்கர் ஆகும். சாதாரண ரத்த அழுத்தம் 120/80 மிமீ பாதரசம். ABO ரத்த வகைகள் மற்றும் Rh காரணி (கார்ல் லேண்ட்ஸ்டீனர் கண்டறிந்தார்).

subject: science
chapter: Unit 14 Transportation in Plants and Circulation in Animals
text:
UNIT 14 TRANSPORTATION IN PLANTS AND CIRCULATION IN ANIMALS

ASCENT OF SAP, TRANSPIRATION PULL, AND ROOT PRESSURE (PAGE 205)

Ascent of sap is the upward translocation of water and dissolved mineral ions from roots to foliage through xylem conduits against gravity. Mechanisms: 1. Root pressure: active ion uptake creates osmotic hydrostatic pressure pushing water upward in xylem vessels. 2. Transpiration pull theory (Dixon and Joly): evaporation of water vapor through leaf stomata creates huge negative suction tension transmitted throughout continuous xylem water columns, held intact by strong cohesion (intermolecular attraction between water molecules) and adhesion (attraction between water and hydrophilic xylem walls).
text_ta:
Unit 14 Transportation in Plants and Circulation in Animals

Ascent of Sap, Transpiration Pull, and Root Pressure (பக்கம் 205)

தாவரங்களில் சாறேற்றம் மற்றும் நீராவிப்போக்கு: சைலம் வழியே நீர் மேல்நோக்கிச் செல்லும் சாறேற்றம். டிக்சன் மற்றும் ஜாலி கொள்கை: நீராவிப்போக்கு இழுவிசை, நீரின் கூட்டிணைவு (Cohesion) மற்றும் ஒட்டிணைவு (Adhesion) பண்புகளால் நீர் தொடர்ந்து மேல்நோக்கி இழுக்கப்படுகிறது.

subject: science
chapter: Unit 14 Transportation in Plants and Circulation in Animals
text:
UNIT 14 TRANSPORTATION IN PLANTS AND CIRCULATION IN ANIMALS

BLOOD COMPOSITION: PLASMA, RBC, WBC, AND PLATELETS (PAGE 206)

Blood is a fluid connective tissue consisting of plasma (55%) and formed cellular elements (45%). Plasma is pale yellow alkaline fluid containing albumin, globulin, fibrinogen, and electrolytes. Formed elements: 1. Red blood cells (Erythrocytes): biconcave enucleated discs containing iron-rich haemoglobin for respiratory gas transport (lifespan ~ 120 days). 2. White blood cells (Leukocytes): nucleated defense cells comprising granulocytes (neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils) and agranulocytes (lymphocytes producing antibodies and phagocytic monocytes). 3. Blood platelets (Thrombocytes): non-nucleated fragments releasing thromboplastin to trigger blood clotting at wound sites.
text_ta:
Unit 14 Transportation in Plants and Circulation in Animals

Blood Composition: Plasma, RBC, WBC, and Platelets (பக்கம் 206)

ரத்தத்தின் கூறுகள்: பிளாஸ்மா (55%) மற்றும் ரத்த செல்கள் (45%). ரத்த சிவப்பணுக்கள் (எரித்ரோசைட்டுகள்: ஹீமோகுளோபின் மூலம் ஆக்ஸிஜனைக் கடத்துகின்றன), ரத்த வெள்ளை அணுக்கள் (லூக்கோசைட்டுகள்: உடலின் நோய் எதிர்ப்பு மண்டலம்), ரத்த தட்டணுக்கள் (துரோம்போசைட்டுகள்: ரத்தம் உறைதலுக்கு உதவுகின்றன).

chapter: Unit 14 Transportation in Plants and Circulation in Animals
text:
UNIT 14 TRANSPORTATION IN PLANTS AND CIRCULATION IN ANIMALS

DOUBLE CIRCULATION, BLOOD PRESSURE, AND BLOOD GROUPS (PAGE 212)

Human circulation is completely double: 1. Pulmonary circulation: deoxygenated blood pumped from right ventricle to lungs for oxygenation and returns to left atrium. 2. Systemic circulation: oxygenated blood pumped from left ventricle through aorta to systemic tissues and deoxygenated blood returns to right atrium via vena cavae. Pacemaker Sinoatrial (SA) node initiates myogenic electrical impulses. Blood pressure measured with sphygmomanometer: normal reading is 120/80 mmHg (systolic/diastolic). Karl Landsteiner discovered ABO blood groups determined by antigens A and B on erythrocytes and antibodies in plasma; Rh factor (+/-) determines Rh compatibility.
text_ta:
Unit 14 Transportation in Plants and Circulation in Animals

Double Circulation, Blood Pressure, and Blood Groups (பக்கம் 212)

இரட்டை ரத்த ஓட்டம், ரத்த அழுத்தம் மற்றும் ரத்த வகைகள்: நுரையீரல் சுற்றோட்டம் மற்றும் உடல் சுற்றோட்டம். சைனோ-ஆரிக்குலார் (SA) கணு இதயத்தின் துடிப்பை உருவாக்கும் பேஸ்மேக்கர் ஆகும். சாதாரண ரத்த அழுத்தம் 120/80 மிமீ பாதரசம். ABO ரத்த வகைகள் மற்றும் Rh காரணி (கார்ல் லேண்ட்ஸ்டீனர் கண்டறிந்தார்).

chapter: Unit 14 Transportation in Plants and Circulation in Animals
text:
UNIT 14 TRANSPORTATION IN PLANTS AND CIRCULATION IN ANIMALS

ASCENT OF SAP, TRANSPIRATION PULL, AND ROOT PRESSURE (PAGE 213)

Ascent of sap is the upward translocation of water and dissolved mineral ions from roots to foliage through xylem conduits against gravity. Mechanisms: 1. Root pressure: active ion uptake creates osmotic hydrostatic pressure pushing water upward in xylem vessels. 2. Transpiration pull theory (Dixon and Joly): evaporation of water vapor through leaf stomata creates huge negative suction tension transmitted throughout continuous xylem water columns, held intact by strong cohesion (intermolecular attraction between water molecules) and adhesion (attraction between water and hydrophilic xylem walls).

Unit 14 Transportation in Plants and Circulation in Animals

Ascent of Sap, Transpiration Pull, and Root Pressure (பக்கம் 213)

தாவரங்களில் சாறேற்றம் மற்றும் நீராவிப்போக்கு: சைலம் வழியே நீர் மேல்நோக்கிச் செல்லும் சாறேற்றம். டிக்சன் மற்றும் ஜாலி கொள்கை: நீராவிப்போக்கு இழுவிசை, நீரின் கூட்டிணைவு (Cohesion) மற்றும் ஒட்டிணைவு (Adhesion) பண்புகளால் நீர் தொடர்ந்து மேல்நோக்கி இழுக்கப்படுகிறது.

text:
UNIT 14 TRANSPORTATION IN PLANTS AND CIRCULATION IN ANIMALS

BLOOD COMPOSITION: PLASMA, RBC, WBC, AND PLATELETS (PAGE 214)

Blood is a fluid connective tissue consisting of plasma (55%) and formed cellular elements (45%). Plasma is pale yellow alkaline fluid containing albumin, globulin, fibrinogen, and electrolytes. Formed elements: 1. Red blood cells (Erythrocytes): biconcave enucleated discs containing iron-rich haemoglobin for respiratory gas transport (lifespan ~ 120 days). 2. White blood cells (Leukocytes): nucleated defense cells comprising granulocytes (neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils) and agranulocytes (lymphocytes producing antibodies and phagocytic monocytes). 3. Blood platelets (Thrombocytes): non-nucleated fragments releasing thromboplastin to trigger blood clotting at wound sites.

Unit 14 Transportation in Plants and Circulation in Animals

Blood Composition: Plasma, RBC, WBC, and Platelets (பக்கம் 214)

ரத்தத்தின் கூறுகள்: பிளாஸ்மா (55%) மற்றும் ரத்த செல்கள் (45%). ரத்த சிவப்பணுக்கள் (எரித்ரோசைட்டுகள்: ஹீமோகுளோபின் மூலம் ஆக்ஸிஜனைக் கடத்துகின்றன), ரத்த வெள்ளை அணுக்கள் (லூக்கோசைட்டுகள்: உடலின் நோய் எதிர்ப்பு மண்டலம்), ரத்த தட்டணுக்கள் (துரோம்போசைட்டுகள்: ரத்தம் உறைதலுக்கு உதவுகின்றன).

chapter: Unit 14 Transportation in Plants and Circulation in Animals
text:
UNIT 14 TRANSPORTATION IN PLANTS AND CIRCULATION IN ANIMALS

HUMAN HEART ANATOMY AND CARDIAC CYCLE (PAGE 215)

Human heart is a hollow muscular organ enclosed within a double-walled fibroserous pericardial sac containing protective pericardial fluid. Four chambers: right and left atria (thin-walled receiving chambers separated by interatrial septum) and right and left ventricles (thick-walled pumping chambers separated by interventricular septum). Atrioventricular valves: Tricuspid valve between right atrium and ventricle; Bicuspid (mitral) valve between left atrium and ventricle. Semilunar valves guard pulmonary artery and systemic aorta openings. Cardiac cycle (~0.8 s) comprises atrial systole (0.1 s), ventricular systole (0.3 s), and complete cardiac diastole (0.4 s).

chapter: Unit 15 Nervous System
text:
UNIT 15 NERVOUS SYSTEM

CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM: BRAIN MENINGES AND LOBES (PAGE 218)

Central Nervous System (CNS) consists of the brain and spinal cord protected by three cranial meninges: outer dura mater (tough fibrous), middle arachnoid mater (delicate web-like), and inner pia mater (highly vascular). Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) fills the subarachnoid space and cerebral ventricles, cushioning against mechanical shock and regulating cranial hydrostatic pressure. Forebrain comprises cerebrum (two hemispheres linked by corpus callosum; outer cerebral cortex of grey matter folded into gyri and sulci for sensory perception, speech, memory, and voluntary thought) and diencephalon (thalamus sensory relay center and hypothalamus regulating body temperature, thirst, and hunger).
text_ta:
Unit 15 Nervous System

Central Nervous System: Brain Meninges and Lobes (பக்கம் 218)

மைய நரம்பு மண்டலம் மற்றும் மூளையின் அமைப்புகள்: மூளையைச் சுற்றியுள்ள மூன்று சவ்வுகள்: டியூரா மேட்டர், அரக்னாய்டு மேட்டர் மற்றும் பையா மேட்டர். மூளைத் தண்டுவட திரவம் (CSF) அதிர்வுகளிலிருந்து பாதுகாக்கிறது. பெருமூளை (கார்ப்பஸ் கலோசம் மூலம் இணைக்கப்பட்ட இரு அரைக்கோளங்கள்), தலாமஸ் மற்றும் ஹைபோதலாமஸ்.

subject: science
chapter: Unit 15 Nervous System
text:
UNIT 15 NERVOUS SYSTEM

BRAINSTEM: MIDBRAIN, PONS, AND MEDULLA OBLONGATA (PAGE 219)

Midbrain contains four rounded dorsal swellings called corpora quadrigemina coordinating visual and auditory reflex orientations. Hindbrain comprises: 1. Cerebellum: coordinates voluntary muscular posture, equilibrium balance, and motor movements. 2. Pons Varolii: bridge connecting cerebellum hemispheres and medulla, containing pneumatic centers regulating respiratory rhythms. 3. Medulla oblongata: posterior part of brain connecting to the spinal cord, containing vital involuntary autonomic reflex centers: cardiac center (heart rate), vasomotor center (blood vessel diameter), and respiratory center, alongside non-vital reflex centers for vomiting, sneezing, and coughing.
text_ta:
Unit 15 Nervous System

Brainstem: Midbrain, Pons, and Medulla Oblongata (பக்கம் 219)

பின்மூளை மற்றும் முகுளம்: சிறுமூளை (உடலின் சமநிலை மற்றும் இயக்கங்களை ஒருங்கிணைக்கிறது), பா Pons மற்றும் முகுளம் (Medulla oblongata: இதயத் துடிப்பு, சுவாசம் மற்றும் ரத்தக் குழாய் சுருக்கம் போன்ற அனிச்சைச் செயல்களைக் கட்டுப்படுத்துகிறது).

subject: science
chapter: Unit 15 Nervous System
text:
UNIT 15 NERVOUS SYSTEM

REFLEX ACTION, REFLEX ARC, AND AUTONOMIC SYSTEM (PAGE 220)

A reflex action is an involuntary, spontaneous, automatic motor response to a sensory stimulus carried out without conscious cortical intervention. Reflex arc is the neural anatomical pathway: Receptor organ (detects stimulus) -> Afferent sensory neuron -> Spinal cord interneuron (relay center) -> Efferent motor neuron -> Effector muscle/gland (executes rapid motor withdrawal). Peripheral nervous system consists of 12 pairs of cranial nerves and 31 pairs of spinal nerves. Autonomic nervous system (ANS) comprises sympathetic system (fight-or-flight: dilates pupils, elevates heart rate) and parasympathetic system (rest-and-digest: constricts pupils, restores basal calm).
text_ta:
Unit 15 Nervous System

Reflex Action, Reflex Arc, and Autonomic System (பக்கம் 220)

அனிச்சைச் செயல் மற்றும் அனிச்சைச் செயல் வில்: தன்னிச்சையற்ற மற்றும் உடனடி செயல். அனிச்சைச் செயல் வில் பாதை: உணர்வேற்பி -> உணர்ச்சி நரம்பு -> தண்டுவடம் -> இயக்க நரம்பு -> தசைகள். தானியங்கு நரம்பு மண்டலம்: பரிவு நரம்பு மண்டலம் மற்றும் எதிர்ப்பரிவு நரம்பு மண்டலம்.

subject: science
chapter: Unit 15 Nervous System
text:
UNIT 15 NERVOUS SYSTEM

NEURON STRUCTURE AND NERVE IMPULSE CONDUCTION (PAGE 221)

The neuron (nerve cell) is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system. Structure comprises: 1. Cyton (cell body or soma) with central spherical nucleus, neuroplasm, and Nissl granules (ribosome clusters). 2. Dendrites: short, highly branched cytoplasmic processes transmitting sensory impulses towards the cyton. 3. Axon: single long cylindrical nerve fiber transmitting electrical action potentials away from the cyton, insulated by myelin sheath produced by Schwann cells with periodic unmyelinated Nodes of Ranvier facilitating saltatory conduction. Synapse is the microscopic junctional gap where neurotransmitters (acetylcholine) transmit chemical impulses across synaptic clefts.
text_ta:
Unit 15 Nervous System

Neuron Structure and Nerve Impulse Conduction (பக்கம் 221)

நியூரான் அமைப்பு மற்றும் நரம்புத் தூண்டல்: நியூரானின் மூன்று முக்கிய பகுதிகள்: சைட்டான் (உடல்), டென்ட்ரைட்டுகள் (உட்புகும் இழைகள்) மற்றும் ஆக்சான் (வெளிச்செல்லும் நீள் இழை). மயலின் உறை மற்றும் ரான்வியர் கணுக்கள் நரம்புத் தூண்டலை வேகமாக கடத்துகின்றன. சினாப்ஸ் (Synapse) நரம்பு இணைவுப் பகுதி ஆகும்.

அனிச்சைச் செயல் மற்றும் அனிச்சைச் செயல் வில்: தன்னிச்சையற்ற மற்றும் உடனடி செயல். அனிச்சைச் செயல் வில் பாதை: உணர்வேற்பி -> உணர்ச்சி நரம்பு -> தண்டுவடம் -> இயக்க நரம்பு -> தசைகள். தானியங்கு நரம்பு மண்டலம்: பரிவு நரம்பு மண்டலம் மற்றும் எதிர்ப்பரிவு நரம்பு மண்டலம்.

subject: science
chapter: Unit 15 Nervous System
text:
UNIT 15 NERVOUS SYSTEM

NEURON STRUCTURE AND NERVE IMPULSE CONDUCTION (PAGE 225)

The neuron (nerve cell) is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system. Structure comprises: 1. Cyton (cell body or soma) with central spherical nucleus, neuroplasm, and Nissl granules (ribosome clusters). 2. Dendrites: short, highly branched cytoplasmic processes transmitting sensory impulses towards the cyton. 3. Axon: single long cylindrical nerve fiber transmitting electrical action potentials away from the cyton, insulated by myelin sheath produced by Schwann cells with periodic unmyelinated Nodes of Ranvier facilitating saltatory conduction. Synapse is the microscopic junctional gap where neurotransmitters (acetylcholine) transmit chemical impulses across synaptic clefts.

Unit 15 Nervous System

Neuron Structure and Nerve Impulse Conduction (பக்கம் 225)

நியூரான் அமைப்பு மற்றும் நரம்புத் தூண்டல்: நியூரானின் மூன்று முக்கிய பகுதிகள்: சைட்டான் (உடல்), டென்ட்ரைட்டுகள் (உட்புகும் இழைகள்) மற்றும் ஆக்சான் (வெளிச்செல்லும் நீள் இழை). மயலின் உறை மற்றும் ரான்வியர் கணுக்கள் நரம்புத் தூண்டலை வேகமாக கடத்துகின்றன. சினாப்ஸ் (Synapse) நரம்பு இணைவுப் பகுதி ஆகும்.

subject: science
chapter: Unit 15 Nervous System
text:
UNIT 15 NERVOUS SYSTEM

CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM: BRAIN MENINGES AND LOBES (PAGE 226)

Central Nervous System (CNS) consists of the brain and spinal cord protected by three cranial meninges: outer dura mater (tough fibrous), middle arachnoid mater (delicate web-like), and inner pia mater (highly vascular). Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) fills the subarachnoid space and cerebral ventricles, cushioning against mechanical shock and regulating cranial hydrostatic pressure. Forebrain comprises cerebrum (two hemispheres linked by corpus callosum; outer cerebral cortex of grey matter folded into gyri and sulci for sensory perception, speech, memory, and voluntary thought) and diencephalon (thalamus sensory relay center and hypothalamus regulating body temperature, thirst, and hunger).

Unit 15 Nervous System

Central Nervous System: Brain Meninges and Lobes (பக்கம் 226)

மைய நரம்பு மண்டலம் மற்றும் மூளையின் அமைப்புகள்: மூளையைச் சுற்றியுள்ள மூன்று சவ்வுகள்: டியூரா மேட்டர், அரக்னாய்டு மேட்டர் மற்றும் பையா மேட்டர். மூளைத் தண்டுவட திரவம் (CSF) அதிர்வுகளிலிருந்து பாதுகாக்கிறது. பெருமூளை (கார்ப்பஸ் கலோசம் மூலம் இணைக்கப்பட்ட இரு அரைக்கோளங்கள்), தலாமஸ் மற்றும் ஹைபோதலாமஸ்.

subject: science
chapter: Unit 15 Nervous System
text:
UNIT 15 NERVOUS SYSTEM

BRAINSTEM: MIDBRAIN, PONS, AND MEDULLA OBLONGATA (PAGE 227)

Midbrain contains four rounded dorsal swellings called corpora quadrigemina coordinating visual and auditory reflex orientations. Hindbrain comprises: 1. Cerebellum: coordinates voluntary muscular posture, equilibrium balance, and motor movements. 2. Pons Varolii: bridge connecting cerebellum hemispheres and medulla, containing pneumatic centers regulating respiratory rhythms. 3. Medulla oblongata: posterior part of brain connecting to the spinal cord, containing vital involuntary autonomic reflex centers: cardiac center (heart rate), vasomotor center (blood vessel diameter), and respiratory center, alongside non-vital reflex centers for vomiting, sneezing, and coughing.

Brainstem: Midbrain, Pons, and Medulla Oblongata (பக்கம் 227)

பின்மூளை மற்றும் முகுளம்: சிறுமூளை (உடலின் சமநிலை மற்றும் இயக்கங்களை ஒருங்கிணைக்கிறது), பா Pons மற்றும் முகுளம் (Medulla oblongata: இதயத் துடிப்பு, சுவாசம் மற்றும் ரத்தக் குழாய் சுருக்கம் போன்ற அனிச்சைச் செயல்களைக் கட்டுப்படுத்துகிறது).

subject: science
chapter: Unit 15 Nervous System
text:
UNIT 15 NERVOUS SYSTEM

REFLEX ACTION, REFLEX ARC, AND AUTONOMIC SYSTEM (PAGE 228)

A reflex action is an involuntary, spontaneous, automatic motor response to a sensory stimulus carried out without conscious cortical intervention. Reflex arc is the neural anatomical pathway: Receptor organ (detects stimulus) -> Afferent sensory neuron -> Spinal cord interneuron (relay center) -> Efferent motor neuron -> Effector muscle/gland (executes rapid motor withdrawal). Peripheral nervous system consists of 12 pairs of cranial nerves and 31 pairs of spinal nerves. Autonomic nervous system (ANS) comprises sympathetic system (fight-or-flight: dilates pupils, elevates heart rate) and parasympathetic system (rest-and-digest: constricts pupils, restores basal calm).

chapter: Unit 16 Plant and Animal Hormones
text:
UNIT 16 PLANT AND ANIMAL HORMONES

PLANT HORMONES (PHYTOHORMONES): AUXINS AND GIBBERELLINS (PAGE 229)

Phytohormones are organic chemical regulators synthesized in minute concentrations that control plant growth and physiological responses. Auxins (Indole-3-acetic acid IAA) synthesized at shoot apices promote apical dominance (inhibiting lateral bud growth), stimulate phototropism, prevent premature fruit/leaf drop, and induce parthenocarpy (seedless fruit formation). Gibberellins synthesized in young seeds promote rapid stem elongation and bolting (sudden elongation of internodes in rosette plants prior to flowering), break seed and bud dormancy, and induce alpha-amylase synthesis during seed germination.
text_ta:
Unit 16 Plant and Animal Hormones

Plant Hormones (Phytohormones): Auxins and Gibberellins (பக்கம் 229)

தாவர ஹார்மோன்கள்: ஆக்ஸின்கள் மற்றும் ஜிப்ரல்லின்கள்: ஆக்ஸின்கள் (IAA): நுனி ஆதிக்கத்தைத் தூண்டுகின்றன, ஒளிசார் அசைவை ஏற்படுத்துகின்றன மற்றும் விதையிலாக் கனிகளை (Parthenocarpy) உருவாக்குகின்றன. ஜிப்ரல்லின்கள்: கணுவிடைப் பகுதி நீட்சியடைவதைத் (Bolting) தூண்டுகின்றன மற்றும் விதை உறக்கத்தை நீக்குகின்றன.

subject: science
chapter: Unit 16 Plant and Animal Hormones
text:
UNIT 16 PLANT AND ANIMAL HORMONES

CYTOKININS, ABSCISIC ACID, AND ETHYLENE (PAGE 230)

Cytokinins (zeatin, kinetin) are purine-derived hormones synthesized in root tips that promote active cell division (cytokinesis) in the presence of auxin, delay leaf senescence (Richmond-Lang effect by preventing chlorophyll breakdown), and overcome apical dominance to promote lateral bud outgrowth. Abscisic Acid (ABA) is a growth inhibitor known as the stress hormone; it triggers rapid stomatal closure under drought stress, promotes leaf and fruit abscission, and maintains seed dormancy. Ethylene is a gaseous plant hormone synthesized in ripening fruits that accelerates fruit ripening (climacteric rise) and stimulates senescence and abscission.

Unit 16 Plant and Animal Hormones

Cytokinins, Abscisic Acid, and Ethylene (பக்கம் 230)

சைட்டோகைனின், அப்சிசிக் அமிலம் மற்றும் எத்திலீன்: சைட்டோகைனின் செல் பகுப்பைத் தூண்டுகிறது, இலை மூப்படைவதைத் தாமதப்படுத்துகிறது (Richmond-Lang விளைவு). அப்சிசிக் அமிலம் (ABA: மன அழுத்த ஹார்மோன் - வறட்சியில் இலைத்துளைகளை மூடுகிறது). எத்திலீன்: பழங்களை பழுக்க வைக்கும் வாயுநிலை ஹார்மோன்.

subject: science
chapter: Unit 16 Plant and Animal Hormones
text:
UNIT 16 PLANT AND ANIMAL HORMONES

PITUITARY GLAND AND THYROID ENDOCRINE SECRETIONS (PAGE 231)

The pituitary gland (hypophysis, master endocrine gland) is situated at the base of the brain in the sella turcica of the sphenoid bone. Anterior pituitary (adenohypophysis) secretes Growth Hormone GH (deficiency in childhood causes dwarfism; oversecretion causes gigantism, in adults acromegaly), TSH, ACTH, and gonadotropins (FSH, LH). Posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis) releases oxytocin (stimulates uterine contractions during parturition and milk ejection) and Vasopressin / ADH (promotes renal water reabsorption; deficiency leads to diabetes insipidus with frequent urination polyuria). Thyroid gland secretes Thyroxine (T4) regulating Basal Metabolic Rate BMR (iodine deficiency causes Simple Goitre; hypothyroid in infants causes Cretinism; hyperthyroidism causes Graves disease).
text_ta:
Unit 16 Plant and Animal Hormones

Pituitary Gland and Thyroid Endocrine Secretions (பக்கம் 231)

பிட்யூட்டரி மற்றும் தைராய்டு சுரப்பிகள்: பிட்யூட்டரி (தலைமைச் சுரப்பி): வளர்ச்சி ஹார்மோன் (GH), தைராய்டைத் தூண்டும் ஹார்மோன் (TSH), வாசோபிரசின் (ADH: குறைவினால் டயாபடீஸ் இன்சிபிடஸ் ஏற்படுகிறது) மற்றும் ஆக்ஸிடோசின். தைராய்டு சுரப்பி: தைராக்சின் (T4: அடிப்படை வளர்சிதை மாற்றத்தைக் கட்டுப்படுத்துகிறது, அயோடின் குறைவினால் எளிய காய்ட்டர் ஏற்படுகிறது).

subject: science
chapter: Unit 16 Plant and Animal Hormones
text:
UNIT 16 PLANT AND ANIMAL HORMONES

PANCREAS ISLETS OF LANGERHANS AND ADRENAL GLANDS (PAGE 232)

Endocrine pancreas contains Islets of Langerhans: Alpha cells secrete Glucagon (converts liver glycogen to glucose, raising blood sugar); Beta cells secrete Insulin (promotes cellular glucose uptake and glycogenesis, lowering blood sugar; hypo-secretion causes Diabetes Mellitus with hyperglycemia and glucosuria). Adrenal glands sit on top of kidneys: Adrenal cortex secretes mineralocorticoids (aldosterone regulating electrolyte balance) and glucocorticoids (cortisol). Adrenal medulla secretes Catecholamines: Adrenaline (epinephrine) and Noradrenaline (norepinephrine) - the emergency hormones of fight, flight, or fright, rapidly elevating heart rate, arterial blood pressure, and alertness.

Pancreas Islets of Langerhans and Adrenal Glands (பக்கம் 232)

கணையம் மற்றும் அட்ரினல் சுரப்பிகள்: லாங்கர்ஹான் திட்டுகள்: ஆல்ஃபா செல்கள் குளூக்கோகானையும், பீட்டா செல்கள் இன்சுலினையும் சுரக்கின்றன (இன்சுலின் குறைவினால் டயாபடீஸ் மெல்லிடஸ் ஏற்படுகிறது). அட்ரினல் சுரப்பி: அவசரகால ஹார்மோன்கள் அல்லது சண்டை மற்றும் பயமுறுத்தும் ஹார்மோன்கள் (அட்ரினலின் மற்றும் நார்அட்ரினலின்).

UNIT 16 PLANT AND ANIMAL HORMONES

CYTOKININS, ABSCISIC ACID, AND ETHYLENE (PAGE 238)

Cytokinins (zeatin, kinetin) are purine-derived hormones synthesized in root tips that promote active cell division (cytokinesis) in the presence of auxin, delay leaf senescence (Richmond-Lang effect by preventing chlorophyll breakdown), and overcome apical dominance to promote lateral bud outgrowth. text:
UNIT 16 PLANT AND ANIMAL HORMONES

PITUITARY GLAND AND THYROID ENDOCRINE SECRETIONS (PAGE 239)

The pituitary gland (hypophysis, master endocrine gland) is situated at the base of the brain in the sella turcica of the sphenoid bone. Anterior pituitary (adenohypophysis) secretes Growth Hormone GH (deficiency in childhood causes dwarfism; oversecretion causes gigantism, in adults acromegaly), TSH, ACTH, and gonadotropins (FSH, LH). Posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis) releases oxytocin (stimulates uterine contractions during parturition and milk ejection) and Vasopressin / ADH (promotes renal water reabsorption; deficiency leads to diabetes insipidus with frequent urination polyuria). Thyroid gland secretes Thyroxine (T4) regulating Basal Metabolic Rate BMR (iodine deficiency causes Simple Goitre; hypothyroid in infants causes Cretinism; hyperthyroidism causes Graves disease).

text:
UNIT 16 PLANT AND ANIMAL HORMONES

PANCREAS ISLETS OF LANGERHANS AND ADRENAL GLANDS (PAGE 240)

Endocrine pancreas contains Islets of Langerhans: Alpha cells secrete Glucagon (converts liver glycogen to glucose, raising blood sugar); Beta cells secrete Insulin (promotes cellular glucose uptake and glycogenesis, lowering blood sugar; hypo-secretion causes Diabetes Mellitus with hyperglycemia and glucosuria). Adrenal glands sit on top of kidneys: Adrenal cortex secretes mineralocorticoids (aldosterone regulating electrolyte balance) and glucocorticoids (cortisol). Adrenal medulla secretes Catecholamines: Adrenaline (epinephrine) and Noradrenaline (norepinephrine) - the emergency hormones of fight, flight, or fright, rapidly elevating heart rate, arterial blood pressure, and alertness.

text:
UNIT 17 REPRODUCTION IN PLANTS AND ANIMALS

HUMAN REPRODUCTIVE ANATOMY: GAMETOGENESIS AND MENSTRUAL CYCLE (PAGE 243)

Male reproductive system comprises paired testes in scrotal sac (producing testosterone in Leydig cells and spermatozoa in seminiferous tubules via spermatogenesis), epididymis, vas deferens, and accessory glands (seminal vesicles, prostate, bulbourethral). Female system comprises ovaries (producing estrogen/progesterone and ova via oogenesis), Fallopian tubes (site of fertilization), uterus (womb with endometrium), and vagina. Menstrual cycle (~28 days) comprises: follicular phase (FSH stimulates follicle growth), ovulatory phase (LH surge triggers ovulation around day 14), luteal phase (corpus luteum secretes progesterone), and menstrual flow phase (endometrial shedding).

Unit 17 Reproduction in Plants and Animals

Human Reproductive Anatomy: Gametogenesis and Menstrual Cycle (பக்கம் 243)

மனித இனப்பெருக்க மண்டலம் மற்றும் மாதவிடாய் சுழற்சி: ஆண் மற்றும் பெண் இனப்பெருக்க உறுப்புகள். விந்து உருவாக்கம் மற்றும் அண்ட உருவாக்கம். அண்டவிடுப்பு (Ovulation) LH ஹார்மோன் எழுச்சியால் 14-ஆம் நாளில் நிகழ்கிறது. புரோஜெஸ்டிரான் கருவுறுதலுக்கான கருப்பையைத் தயார் செய்கிறது.

subject: science
chapter: Unit 17 Reproduction in Plants and Animals
text:
UNIT 17 REPRODUCTION IN PLANTS AND ANIMALS

EMBRYONIC DEVELOPMENT, PLACENTA, AND REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH (PAGE 244)

Fertilization occurs in the ampullary-isthmic junction of the Fallopian tube. Zygote undergoes rapid cleavage divisions: blastomeres form solid morula, then hollow blastocyst. Blastocyst implants into vascular uterine endometrium around day 7 post-fertilization. The placenta is a temporary structural and physiological disc formed by maternal uterine wall and fetal chorionic villi, providing respiratory gas exchange, nutrient delivery, and waste excretion. Gestation period in humans lasts approximately 280 days (40 weeks). Reproductive health encompasses contraception methods (barrier condoms, IUD copper-T, hormonal pills, and surgical vasectomy/tubectomy) preventing sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and unwanted pregnancy.
text_ta:
Unit 17 Reproduction in Plants and Animals

Embryonic Development, Placenta, and Reproductive Health (பக்கம் 244)

கருவளர்ச்சி, நஞ்சுக்கொடி மற்றும் இனப்பெருக்க சுகாதாரம்: கருவுறுதல் ஃபெலோபியன் குழாயில் நிகழ்கிறது. நஞ்சுக்கொடி (Placenta) தாய்க்கும் சேய்க்கும் இடையே ஊட்டச்சத்து மற்றும் வாயுப் பரிமாற்றத்தை உறுதி செய்கிறது. மனித கருவுறுதல் காலம் 280 நாட்கள். குடும்பக் கட்டுப்பாடு முறைகள்: காண்டம், காப்பர்-T, வாசக்டமி மற்றும் டியூபக்டமி.

chapter: Unit 17 Reproduction in Plants and Animals
text:
UNIT 17 REPRODUCTION IN PLANTS AND ANIMALS

FLOWER STRUCTURE AND POLLINATION MODES (PAGE 245)

A complete angiosperm flower has four whorls: non-essential perianth whorls (calyx of sepals and corolla of petals) and essential reproductive whorls (androecium of stamens and gynoecium of carpels). Stamen comprises anther (contains microsporangia producing pollen grains) and filament. Carpel comprises stigma, style, and basal ovary housing ovules. Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from anther to stigma: 1. Self-pollination (Autogamy): transfer within same flower or plant. 2. Cross-pollination (Allogamy): transfer between different flowers of same species mediated by agents: wind (Anemophily), insects (Entomophily), water (Hydrophily), or birds (Ornithophily).

மலரின் பாகங்கள் மற்றும் மகரந்தச்சேர்க்கை: மலரின் நான்கு வட்டங்கள்: புல்லி வட்டம், அல்லி வட்டம், மகரந்தத்தாள் வட்டம் (ஆண் பகுதி) மற்றும் சூலக வட்டம் (பெண் பகுதி). மகரந்தச்சேர்க்கை: தன் மகரந்தச்சேர்க்கை மற்றும் அயல் மகரந்தச்சேர்க்கை (காற்று, பூச்சிகள் மற்றும் நீர் மூலம் நிகழ்கிறது).

subject: science
chapter: Unit 17 Reproduction in Plants and Animals
text:
UNIT 17 REPRODUCTION IN PLANTS AND ANIMALS

DOUBLE FERTILIZATION AND SEED FORMATION (PAGE 246)

In angiosperms, a pollen grain germinates on the receptive stigma, producing a pollen tube that grows down the style towards the micropyle of the ovule. The generative nucleus divides into two male gametes. Inside the embryo sac, Double Fertilization occurs: 1. Syngamy: one male gamete (n) fuses with the haploid egg nucleus (n) to form the diploid zygote (2n), developing into the embryo. 2. Triple fusion: the second male gamete (n) fuses with the diploid secondary nucleus (2n) to form the triploid Primary Endosperm Nucleus PEN (3n), developing into nutrient-rich endosperm tissue. Ovule matures into seed; ovary transforms into fruit.

Double Fertilization and Seed Formation (பக்கம் 246)

இரட்டைக்கருவுறுதல் மற்றும் மூவிணைவு: மகரந்தக் குழாய் மூலம் இரு ஆண் கேமிட்டுகள் உள்ளே நுழைகின்றன. ஒரு ஆண் கேமிட் அண்டத்துடன் இணைந்து இருமடிய சைகோட்டை உருவாக்குகிறது (Syngamy). மற்றொரு ஆண் கேமிட் துருவ உட்கருக்களுடன் இணைந்து மும்மடிய எண்டோஸ்பெர்மத்தை உருவாக்குகிறது (Triple fusion). சூல் விதையாகவும் சூற்பை கனியாகவும் மாறுகிறது.

DOUBLE FERTILIZATION AND SEED FORMATION (PAGE 250)

Syngamy: one male gamete (n) fuses with the haploid egg nucleus (n) to form the diploid zygote (2n), developing into the embryo. 2. Triple fusion: the second male gamete (n) fuses with the diploid secondary nucleus (2n) to form the triploid Primary Endosperm Nucleus PEN (3n), developing into nutrient-rich endosperm tissue. UNIT 17 REPRODUCTION IN PLANTS AND ANIMALS

HUMAN REPRODUCTIVE ANATOMY: GAMETOGENESIS AND MENSTRUAL CYCLE (PAGE 251)

Male reproductive system comprises paired testes in scrotal sac (producing testosterone in Leydig cells and spermatozoa in seminiferous tubules via spermatogenesis), epididymis, vas deferens, and accessory glands (seminal vesicles, prostate, bulbourethral). Female system comprises ovaries (producing estrogen/progesterone and ova via oogenesis), Fallopian tubes (site of fertilization), uterus (womb with endometrium), and vagina. Menstrual cycle (~28 days) comprises: follicular phase (FSH stimulates follicle growth), ovulatory phase (LH surge triggers ovulation around day 14), luteal phase (corpus luteum secretes progesterone), and menstrual flow phase (endometrial shedding).

chapter: Unit 17 Reproduction in Plants and Animals
text:
UNIT 17 REPRODUCTION IN PLANTS AND ANIMALS

EMBRYONIC DEVELOPMENT, PLACENTA, AND REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH (PAGE 252)

Fertilization occurs in the ampullary-isthmic junction of the Fallopian tube. Zygote undergoes rapid cleavage divisions: blastomeres form solid morula, then hollow blastocyst. Blastocyst implants into vascular uterine endometrium around day 7 post-fertilization. The placenta is a temporary structural and physiological disc formed by maternal uterine wall and fetal chorionic villi, providing respiratory gas exchange, nutrient delivery, and waste excretion. Gestation period in humans lasts approximately 280 days (40 weeks). Reproductive health encompasses contraception methods (barrier condoms, IUD copper-T, hormonal pills, and surgical vasectomy/tubectomy) preventing sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and unwanted pregnancy.

கருவளர்ச்சி, நஞ்சுக்கொடி மற்றும் இனப்பெருக்க சுகாதாரம்: கருவுறுதல் ஃபெலோபியன் குழாயில் நிகழ்கிறது. நஞ்சுக்கொடி (Placenta) தாய்க்கும் சேய்க்கும் இடையே ஊட்டச்சத்து மற்றும் வாயுப் பரிமாற்றத்தை உறுதி செய்கிறது. மனித கருவுறுதல் காலம் 280 நாட்கள். குடும்பக் கட்டுப்பாடு முறைகள்: காண்டம், காப்பர்-T, வாசக்டமி மற்றும் டியூபக்டமி.

குரோமோசோம் அமைப்பு மற்றும் DNA இரட்டைச் சுருள் மாதிரி: சென்ட்ரோமியர் அடிப்படையில் குரோமோசோம்கள்: மெட்டாசென்ட்ரிக், சப்-மெட்டாசென்ட்ரிக், அக்ரோசென்ட்ரிக் மற்றும் டீலோசென்ட்ரிக். வாட்சன் மற்றும் கிரிக் DNA இரட்டைச் சுருள் மாதிரி: அடினைன் தயமினுடன் 2 ஹைட்ரஜன் பிணைப்புகளாலும் (A=T), குவானைன் சைட்டோசினுடன் 3 ஹைட்ரஜன் பிணைப்புகளாலும் (G=C) இணைகின்றன.

subject: science
chapter: Unit 18 Heredity
text:
UNIT 18 HEREDITY

MENDELIAN GENETICS: MONOHYBRID AND DIHYBRID CROSS (PAGE 273)

Gregor Johann Mendel, father of genetics, conducted hybridization experiments on garden pea (Pisum sativum). In a monohybrid cross (studying one trait like plant height: Tall TT x Dwarf tt), F1 generation showed all Tall (Tt). F2 generation produced phenotypic ratio 3 Tall : 1 Dwarf (3:1) and genotypic ratio 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt (1:2:1), proving Mendel Law of Segregation (alleles separate cleanly during gamete formation). In a dihybrid cross (studying two traits: Round Yellow RRYY x Wrinkled Green rryy), F2 produced phenotypic ratio 9:3:3:1, establishing Mendel Law of Independent Assortment.
text_ta:
Unit 18 Heredity

Mendelian Genetics: Monohybrid and Dihybrid Cross (பக்கம் 273)

மெண்டலின் மரபியல்: ஒரு பண்பு மற்றும் இரு பண்புக் கலப்பு: கிரிகோர் மெண்டல் பட்டாணிச் செடியில் ஆய்வு செய்தார். ஒரு பண்புக் கலப்பு F2 புறத்தோற்ற விகிதம் 3:1 மற்றும் மரபணு விகிதம் 1:2:1 (பிரிதல் விதி). இரு பண்புக் கலப்பு புறத்தோற்ற விகிதம் 9:3:3:1 (சார்பின்றி ஒதுங்குதல் விதி).

chapter: Unit 19 Origin and Evolution of Life
text:
UNIT 19 ORIGIN AND EVOLUTION OF LIFE

EVIDENCES OF EVOLUTION: HOMOLOGOUS AND ANALOGOUS ORGANS (PAGE 274)

Homologous organs possess identical fundamental anatomical structure and embryonic origin but perform different functions in different species, proving divergent evolution (e.g., forelimb of human, flipper of whale, wing of bat). Analogous organs perform similar functions in unrelated species but possess completely different anatomical architecture and origins, proving convergent evolution (e.g., wings of birds and wings of insects). Vestigial organs are non-functional remnants in modern organisms that were fully functional in evolutionary ancestors (e.g., human tailbone coccyx, plica semilunaris).
text_ta:
Unit 19 Origin and Evolution of Life

Evidences of Evolution: Homologous and Analogous Organs (பக்கம் 274)

பரிணாமத்திற்கான சான்றுகள்: அமைப்பொத்த உறுப்புகள் (Homologous organs: மனிதனின் கை மற்றும் திமிங்கலத்தின் துடுப்பு - விரி பரிணாமம்). செயலொத்த உறுப்புகள் (Analogous organs: பூச்சியின் சிறகுகள் மற்றும் பறவையின் சிறகுகள் - குவி பரிணாமம்). எச்ச உறுப்புகள் (மனிதனின் வால் எலும்பு, குடல்வால்).

chapter: Unit 19 Origin and Evolution of Life
text:
UNIT 19 ORIGIN AND EVOLUTION OF LIFE

THEORIES OF EVOLUTION: LAMARCKISM AND DARWINISM (PAGE 275)

Jean-Baptiste Lamarck proposed inheritance of acquired characters through the Principle of Use and Disuse (e.g., giraffe elongated neck evolved by continuous stretching across generations; vestigial organs like human vermiform appendix shrank from disuse). Charles Darwin proposed the Theory of Natural Selection in On the Origin of Species based on overproduction, struggle for existence, universal variation, survival of the fittest (Herbert Spencer phrase), and natural selection driving speciation over geological timescales.

Unit 19 Origin and Evolution of Life

பரிணாமக் கோட்பாடுகள்: லாமார்க் மற்றும் டார்வின்: லாமார்க்கின் பயன்பாடு மற்றும் பயன்படாமைக் கோட்பாடு (ஒட்டகச்சிவிங்கியின் நீண்ட கழுத்து). சார்லஸ் டார்வினின் இயற்கை தேர்வு கோட்பாடு: அதிக உற்பத்தி, வாழ்க்கைக்கான போராட்டம், மாறுபாடுகள் மற்றும் தகவமைப்பு மூலம் புதிய சிற்றினங்கள் உருவாதல்.

பரிணாமக் கோட்பாடுகள்: லாமார்க் மற்றும் டார்வின்: லாமார்க்கின் பயன்பாடு மற்றும் பயன்படாமைக் கோட்பாடு (ஒட்டகச்சிவிங்கியின் நீண்ட கழுத்து). சார்லஸ் டார்வினின் இயற்கை தேர்வு கோட்பாடு: அதிக உற்பத்தி, வாழ்க்கைக்கான போராட்டம், மாறுபாடுகள் மற்றும் தகவமைப்பு மூலம் புதிய சிற்றினங்கள் உருவாதல்.

subject: science
chapter: Unit 19 Origin and Evolution of Life
text:
UNIT 19 ORIGIN AND EVOLUTION OF LIFE

EVIDENCES OF EVOLUTION: HOMOLOGOUS AND ANALOGOUS ORGANS (PAGE 286)

Homologous organs possess identical fundamental anatomical structure and embryonic origin but perform different functions in different species, proving divergent evolution (e.g., forelimb of human, flipper of whale, wing of bat). Analogous organs perform similar functions in unrelated species but possess completely different anatomical architecture and origins, proving convergent evolution (e.g., wings of birds and wings of insects). Vestigial organs are non-functional remnants in modern organisms that were fully functional in evolutionary ancestors (e.g., human tailbone coccyx, plica semilunaris).

Unit 19 Origin and Evolution of Life

Evidences of Evolution: Homologous and Analogous Organs (பக்கம் 286)

பரிணாமத்திற்கான சான்றுகள்: அமைப்பொத்த உறுப்புகள் (Homologous organs: மனிதனின் கை மற்றும் திமிங்கலத்தின் துடுப்பு - விரி பரிணாமம்). செயலொத்த உறுப்புகள் (Analogous organs: பூச்சியின் சிறகுகள் மற்றும் பறவையின் சிறகுகள் - குவி பரிணாமம்). எச்ச உறுப்புகள் (மனிதனின் வால் எலும்பு, குடல்வால்).

chapter: Unit 20 Breeding and Biotechnology
text:
UNIT 20 BREEDING AND BIOTECHNOLOGY

PLANT AND ANIMAL BREEDING METHODOLOGIES (PAGE 287)

Breeding is the purposeful manipulation of plant and animal genomes to create varieties with desirable agronomic traits, high yields, and disease resistance. Plant breeding steps: collection of genetic variability, evaluation, hybridization between chosen parents, and selection. Green Revolution pioneered by Dr. Norman Borlaug and Dr. M.S. Swaminathan introduced semi-dwarf high-yielding wheat (Sonalika) and rice (IR8) varieties. Animal breeding involves inbreeding (mating closely related individuals for 4-6 generations to increase homozygosity) and outbreeding (crossbreeding, outcrossing) to produce heterosis (hybrid vigour).
text_ta:
Unit 20 Breeding and Biotechnology

Plant and Animal Breeding Methodologies (பக்கம் 287)

பயிர்ப்பெருக்கம் மற்றும் விலங்குப் பெருக்கம்: பசுமைப் புரட்சி (டாக்டர் எம்.எஸ். சுவாமிநாதன் - அதிக விளைச்சல் தரும் நெல் மற்றும் கோதுமை ரகங்கள்). கலப்பின வீரியம் (Heterosis). தாவரப் பெருக்கம் மூலம் நோய் எதிர்ப்பு மற்றும் வறட்சி தாங்கும் ரகங்கள் உருவாக்கப்படுகின்றன.

subject: science
chapter: Unit 20 Breeding and Biotechnology
text:
UNIT 20 BREEDING AND BIOTECHNOLOGY

GENETIC ENGINEERING, RDNA TECHNOLOGY, AND APPLICATIONS (PAGE 288)

Recombinant DNA (rDNA) technology (genetic engineering) cuts and splices genetic material across species boundaries. Key tools: Restriction endonucleases (molecular scissors) that recognize and cleave specific palindromic DNA sequences; DNA ligase (molecular glue) that seals phosphodiester backbones; and cloning vectors (plasmids like pBR322) that deliver donor genes into host bacteria. Applications: mass production of human recombinant insulin (Humulin), genetically modified pest-resistant crops (Bt cotton expressing Bacillus thuringiensis endotoxin), and gene therapy for genetic diseases.
text_ta:
Unit 20 Breeding and Biotechnology

Genetic Engineering, rDNA Technology, and Applications (பக்கம் 288)

மரபணுப் பொறியியல் மற்றும் மறுசேர்க்கை DNA தொழில்நுட்பம்: மூலக்கூறு கத்தரிக்கோல் (கட்டுப்படுத்தும் எண்டோநியூக்ளியேஸ் நொதிகள்), மூலக்கூறு பசை (DNA லிகேஸ்) மற்றும் பிளாஸ்மிட் கடத்திகள். பயன்கள்: மனித இன்சுலின் (ஹியூமுலின்) தயாரிப்பு, Bt பருத்தி மற்றும் மரபணு சிகிச்சை.

subject: science
chapter: Unit 20 Breeding and Biotechnology
text:
UNIT 20 BREEDING AND BIOTECHNOLOGY

GENETIC ENGINEERING, RDNA TECHNOLOGY, AND APPLICATIONS (PAGE 300)

Recombinant DNA (rDNA) technology (genetic engineering) cuts and splices genetic material across species boundaries. Key tools: Restriction endonucleases (molecular scissors) that recognize and cleave specific palindromic DNA sequences; DNA ligase (molecular glue) that seals phosphodiester backbones; and cloning vectors (plasmids like pBR322) that deliver donor genes into host bacteria. Applications: mass production of human recombinant insulin (Humulin), genetically modified pest-resistant crops (Bt cotton expressing Bacillus thuringiensis endotoxin), and gene therapy for genetic diseases.

chapter: Unit 21 Health and Diseases
text:
UNIT 21 HEALTH AND DISEASES

NON-COMMUNICABLE LIFESTYLE DISORDERS AND IMMUNITY (PAGE 312)

Non-communicable diseases: 1. Diabetes mellitus (type 1 insulin-dependent autoimmune; type 2 non-insulin-dependent metabolic). 2. Cardiovascular diseases: atherosclerosis (cholesterol atheroma plaque in coronary arteries). 3. Cancer (oncology): uncontrolled cellular proliferation forming malignant tumors with metastasis (spread to distant organs via lymph/blood). Carcinogens: tobacco smoke, ionizing UV/X-rays. AIDS caused by Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV, retrovirus attacking CD4+ T-helper lymphocytes, detected by ELISA screening and confirmed by Western Blot). Immunology: innate immunity (skin, lysozyme) and acquired immunity (B-cell humoral antibodies and T-cell cell-mediated immunity).

subject: science
chapter: Unit 21 Health and Diseases
text:
UNIT 21 HEALTH AND DISEASES

COMMUNICABLE PATHOGENIC DISEASES: BACTERIAL, VIRAL, PROTOZOAN (PAGE 313)

Communicable diseases are transmitted from infected hosts to healthy individuals via water, air, food, or vectors. Bacterial diseases: Tuberculosis (Mycobacterium tuberculosis, airborne droplets affecting lungs, BCG vaccine), Typhoid (Salmonella typhi, contaminated food/water, Widal test). Viral diseases: Common cold (Rhinovirus), Hepatitis B (blood-borne serum hepatitis, liver inflammation). Protozoan diseases: Malaria (Plasmodium vivax transmitted by female Anopheles mosquito vector; chill and high fever cycles). Fungal diseases: Ringworm (Microsporum, Trichophyton dermatophytes causing circular skin lesions).

chapter: Unit 22 Environmental Management
text:
UNIT 22 ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT

RENEWABLE AND NON-RENEWABLE ENERGY RESOURCES (PAGE 315)

Energy sources: 1. Non-renewable fossil fuels: coal, crude petroleum, and natural gas formed by anaerobic decomposition of prehistoric biomass under immense geological pressure; combustion emits greenhouse gases (CO2, SO2, NOx) causing acid rain and global warming. 2. Renewable green energy resources: solar energy captured by photovoltaic silicon solar cells; wind energy converted by aerodynamic wind turbines; hydroelectric power from dammed rivers; biomass biogas generated by anaerobic methanogenic bacteria in digesters (containing 65% methane CH4 and 35% CO2).
text_ta:
Unit 22 Environmental Management

Renewable and Non-Renewable Energy Resources (பக்கம் 315)

புதுப்பிக்கத்தக்க மற்றும் புதுப்பிக்க இயலா ஆற்றல் வளங்கள்: நிலக்கரி மற்றும் பெட்ரோலியம் புதுப்பிக்க இயலா புதைபடிவ எரிபொருட்கள் (புவி வெப்பமயமாதலை ஏற்படுத்துகின்றன). புதுப்பிக்கத்தக்க ஆற்றல் வளங்கள்: சூரிய ஆற்றல் (சூரிய மின்கலங்கள்), காற்று ஆற்றல், நீர்மின் ஆற்றல் மற்றும் சாண எரிவாயு (Biogas: 65% மீத்தேன் வாயுவைக் கொண்டுள்ளது).

subject: science
chapter: Unit 22 Environmental Management
text:
UNIT 22 ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT

WASTE MANAGEMENT, CONSERVATION, AND 3R PRINCIPLES (PAGE 316)

Solid waste management requires strict segregation at source into biodegradable organic refuse and non-biodegradable synthetic pollutants (plastics, electronic e-waste). The 3R principle of sustainable living: Reduce consumption, Reuse materials, and Recycle recyclable wastes. Water conservation strategies include rainwater harvesting (recharging subterranean aquifers) and drip/sprinkler micro-irrigation minimizing evaporation loss. Forest conservation requires social forestry, afforestation, prevention of soil erosion, and preservation of wildlife habitats under the Wildlife Protection Act.
text_ta:
Unit 22 Environmental Management

Waste Management, Conservation, and 3R Principles (பக்கம் 316)

கழிவு மேலாண்மை மற்றும் 3R கோட்பாடு: 3R கோட்பாடு: குறைத்தல் (Reduce), மறுபயன்பாடு (Reuse) மற்றும் மறுசுழற்சி (Recycle). மழைநீர் சேகரிப்பு மூலம் நிலத்தடி நீர்மட்டத்தை உயர்த்துதல். காடுகள் மற்றும் வனவிலங்கு பாதுகாப்பு சட்டம்.

UNIT 22 ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT

RENEWABLE AND NON-RENEWABLE ENERGY RESOURCES (PAGE 325)

Energy sources: 1. Non-renewable fossil fuels: coal, crude petroleum, and natural gas formed by anaerobic decomposition of prehistoric biomass under immense geological pressure; combustion emits greenhouse gases (CO2, SO2, NOx) causing acid rain and global warming. 2. Renewable green energy resources: solar energy captured by photovoltaic silicon solar cells; wind energy converted by aerodynamic wind turbines; hydroelectric power from dammed rivers; biomass biogas generated by anaerobic methanogenic bacteria in digesters (containing 65% methane CH4 and 35% CO2).
text_ta:
Unit 22 Environmental Management

Renewable and Non-Renewable Energy Resources (பக்கம் 325)

புதுப்பிக்கத்தக்க மற்றும் புதுப்பிக்க இயலா ஆற்றல் வளங்கள்: நிலக்கரி மற்றும் பெட்ரோலியம் புதுப்பிக்க இயலா புதைபடிவ எரிபொருட்கள் (புவி வெப்பமயமாதலை ஏற்படுத்துகின்றன). புதுப்பிக்கத்தக்க ஆற்றல் வளங்கள்: சூரிய ஆற்றல் (சூரிய மின்கலங்கள்), காற்று ஆற்றல், நீர்மின் ஆற்றல் மற்றும் சாண எரிவாயு (Biogas: 65% மீத்தேன் வாயுவைக் கொண்டுள்ளது).

subject: science
chapter: Unit 22 Environmental Management
text:
UNIT 22 ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT

WASTE MANAGEMENT, CONSERVATION, AND 3R PRINCIPLES (PAGE 326)

Solid waste management requires strict segregation at source into biodegradable organic refuse and non-biodegradable synthetic pollutants (plastics, electronic e-waste). The 3R principle of sustainable living: Reduce consumption, Reuse materials, and Recycle recyclable wastes. Water conservation strategies include rainwater harvesting (recharging subterranean aquifers) and drip/sprinkler micro-irrigation minimizing evaporation loss. Forest conservation requires social forestry, afforestation, prevention of soil erosion, and preservation of wildlife habitats under the Wildlife Protection Act.
text_ta:
Unit 22 Environmental Management

Waste Management, Conservation, and 3R Principles (பக்கம் 326)

கழிவு மேலாண்மை மற்றும் 3R கோட்பாடு: 3R கோட்பாடு: குறைத்தல் (Reduce), மறுபயன்பாடு (Reuse) மற்றும் மறுசுழற்சி (Recycle). மழைநீர் சேகரிப்பு மூலம் நிலத்தடி நீர்மட்டத்தை உயர்த்துதல். காடுகள் மற்றும் வனவிலங்கு பாதுகாப்பு சட்டம்.

subject: science
chapter: Unit 23 Visual Communication
text:
UNIT 23 VISUAL COMMUNICATION

DIGITAL SCRATCH PROGRAMMING AND ANIMATION CONCEPTS (PAGE 327)

Visual communication encompasses computer programming, digital storytelling, and visual graphic design. Scratch is a visual block-based programming language developed by the MIT Media Lab. Key components of Scratch environment: 1. Stage: the backdrop canvas where sprites move and interact. 2. Sprite: characters or graphic objects programmed with motion and actions. 3. Scripts: visual stacks of color-coded interlocking coding blocks (Motion, Looks, Sound, Events, Control, Sensing, Operators, Variables). Creating dynamic loops, conditional decision-making if-then logic, and interactive animations.
text_ta:
Unit 23 Visual Communication

Digital Scratch Programming and Animation Concepts (பக்கம் 327)

காட்சிக் தொடர்பு மற்றும் ஸ்கிராட்ச் (Scratch) மென்பொருள்: கணினி அனிமேஷன் மற்றும் காட்சிக் குறியீட்டு மொழி. ஸ்கிராட்ச் முக்கிய கூறுகள்: மேடை (Stage), ஸ்ப்ரைட் (Sprite - வரைகலை உருவம்) மற்றும் ஸ்கிரிப்ட் (Scripts - வண்ணக் கட்டளைத் தொகுதிகள்). எளிய அனிமேஷன் மற்றும் விளையாட்டுகளை உருவாக்குதல்.

subject: maths
chapter: Chapter 1 Relations and Functions
text:
CHAPTER 1 RELATIONS AND FUNCTIONS

ORDERED PAIRS AND CARTESIAN PRODUCT OF SETS (PAGE 1)

An ordered pair (a, b) consists of two elements specified in a definite strict order where a is the first coordinate and b is the second coordinate: (a, b) = (c, d) if and only if a = c and b = d. The Cartesian product A x B of two non-empty sets A and B is the set of all possible ordered pairs such that the first element belongs to A and the second belongs to B: A x B = {(a, b) : a in A, b in B}. If n(A) = p and n(B) = q, then the cardinal number n(A x B) = p * q. The Cartesian product is non-commutative: A x B != B x A in general, but n(A x B) = n(B x A). Cartesian product of three sets A x B x C forms ordered triplets (a, b, c) representing coordinates in three-dimensional geometric space.
text_ta:
Chapter 1 Relations and Functions

Ordered Pairs and Cartesian Product of Sets (பக்கம் 1)

வரிசைச் சோடிகள் மற்றும் கார்டீசியன் பெருக்கற்பலன்: கார்டீசியன் பெருக்கல் A x B = {(a, b) : a in A, b in B}. n(A) = p மற்றும் n(B) = q எனில், n(A x B) = p * q. பொதுவாக A x B != B x A, ஆனால் n(A x B) = n(B x A).

subject: maths
chapter: Chapter 1 Relations and Functions
text:
CHAPTER 1 RELATIONS AND FUNCTIONS

RELATIONS: DOMAIN, CO-DOMAIN, RANGE, AND TYPES (PAGE 2)

Let A and B be two non-empty sets. A relation R from A to B is a formal mathematical subset of the Cartesian product A x B: R is a subset of A x B. If an ordered pair (a, b) belongs to R, we write a R b (a is related to b). 1. Domain of R = {x in A : (x, y) in R for some y in B}. 2. Co-domain of R is the entire destination set B. 3. Range of R = {y in B : (x, y) in R for some x in A}. The range is always a subset of the co-domain. A null relation contains no elements (R = empty set). Total possible relations from A to B equals 2^(p * q).
text_ta:
Chapter 1 Relations and Functions

Relations: Domain, Co-domain, Range, and Types (பக்கம் 2)

உறவுகள்: மதிப்பகம், துணை மதிப்பகம் மற்றும் வீச்சகம்: A-லிருந்து B-க்கான உறவு R என்பது கார்டீசியன் பெருக்கல் A x B-ன் உட்கணம் ஆகும் (R subset of A x B). உறவின் மதிப்பகம் என்பது R-ல் உள்ள முதல் உறுப்புகளின் கணம்; வீச்சகம் என்பது இரண்டாவது உறுப்புகளின் கணம் ஆகும்.

subject: maths
chapter: Chapter 1 Relations and Functions
text:
CHAPTER 1 RELATIONS AND FUNCTIONS

FUNCTIONS: DEFINITION, ARROW DIAGRAMS, AND VERTICAL LINE TEST (PAGE 3)

A function (or mapping) f from set A to set B (denoted f: A -> B) is a specialized relation wherein every element x in the domain set A is associated with one and only one unique element y in the co-domain set B: y = f(x). Every function is a relation, but not every relation is a function. Representation methods: 1. Set of ordered pairs. 2. Arrow diagram. 3. Table form. 4. Graphical representation. Vertical Line Test: A curve drawn in the XY-plane represents a function if and only if every vertical line intersects the curve at at most one point.
text_ta:

CHAPTER 1 RELATIONS AND FUNCTIONS

TYPES OF FUNCTIONS: ONE-TO-ONE, ONTO, BIJECTION, AND COMPOSITION (PAGE 4)

Classification of functions: 1. One-to-one function (Injective): distinct elements in domain A have distinct unique images in B (f(x1) = f(x2) implies x1 = x2). Tested via Horizontal Line Test. 2. Many-to-one function: two or more domain elements share the same image. 3. Onto function (Surjective): every element in co-domain B is the image of at least one element in domain A (Range = Co-domain). 4. Bijective function: both one-to-one and onto simultaneously; possesses a unique inverse function. Composition of functions: if f: A -> B and g: B -> C, then composite function (g o f)(x) = g(f(x)). Composition is non-commutative (f o g != g o f) but associative ((f o g) o h = f o (g o h)). Linear function f(x) = mx + c, quadratic f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c, cubic f(x) = ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d, and reciprocal function f(x) = 1/x.

CHAPTER 1 RELATIONS AND FUNCTIONS

ORDERED PAIRS AND CARTESIAN PRODUCT OF SETS (PAGE 5)

An ordered pair (a, b) consists of two elements specified in a definite strict order where a is the first coordinate and b is the second coordinate: (a, b) = (c, d) if and only if a = c and b = d. The Cartesian product A x B of two non-empty sets A and B is the set of all possible ordered pairs such that the first element belongs to A and the second belongs to B: A x B = {(a, b) : a in A, b in B}. If n(A) = p and n(B) = q, then the cardinal number n(A x B) = p * q. The Cartesian product is non-commutative: A x B != B x A in general, but n(A x B) = n(B x A). Cartesian product of three sets A x B x C forms ordered triplets (a, b, c) representing coordinates in three-dimensional geometric space.

CHAPTER 1 RELATIONS AND FUNCTIONS

RELATIONS: DOMAIN, CO-DOMAIN, RANGE, AND TYPES (PAGE 6)

Let A and B be two non-empty sets. A relation R from A to B is a formal mathematical subset of the Cartesian product A x B: R is a subset of A x B. If an ordered pair (a, b) belongs to R, we write a R b (a is related to b). 1. Domain of R = {x in A : (x, y) in R for some y in B}. 2. Co-domain of R is the entire destination set B. 3. Range of R = {y in B : (x, y) in R for some x in A}. The range is always a subset of the co-domain. A null relation contains no elements (R = empty set). Total possible relations from A to B equals 2^(p * q).

CHAPTER 1 RELATIONS AND FUNCTIONS

FUNCTIONS: DEFINITION, ARROW DIAGRAMS, AND VERTICAL LINE TEST (PAGE 7)

A function (or mapping) f from set A to set B (denoted f: A -> B) is a specialized relation wherein every element x in the domain set A is associated with one and only one unique element y in the co-domain set B: y = f(x). Every function is a relation, but not every relation is a function. Representation methods: 1. Set of ordered pairs. 2. Arrow diagram. 3. Table form. 4. Graphical representation. Vertical Line Test: A curve drawn in the XY-plane represents a function if and only if every vertical line intersects the curve at at most one point.

CHAPTER 1 RELATIONS AND FUNCTIONS

TYPES OF FUNCTIONS: ONE-TO-ONE, ONTO, BIJECTION, AND COMPOSITION (PAGE 16)

Classification of functions: 1. One-to-one function (Injective): distinct elements in domain A have distinct unique images in B (f(x1) = f(x2) implies x1 = x2). Tested via Horizontal Line Test. 2. Many-to-one function: two or more domain elements share the same image. 3. Onto function (Surjective): every element in co-domain B is the image of at least one element in domain A (Range = Co-domain). 4. Bijective function: both one-to-one and onto simultaneously; possesses a unique inverse function. Composition of functions: if f: A -> B and g: B -> C, then composite function (g o f)(x) = g(f(x)). Composition is non-commutative (f o g != g o f) but associative ((f o g) o h = f o (g o h)). Linear function f(x) = mx + c, quadratic f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c, cubic f(x) = ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d, and reciprocal function f(x) = 1/x.

சார்புகளின் வகைகள் மற்றும் சார்புகளின் சேர்ப்பு: ஒன்றுக்கு ஒன்றான சார்பு (Injective), பலவற்றிற்கு ஒன்றான சார்பு, மேற்கோர்த்தல் சார்பு (Surjective: வீச்சகம் = துணை மதிப்பகம்) மற்றும் இருபுறச் சார்பு (Bijective). சார்புகளின் சேர்ப்பு: (g o f)(x) = g(f(x)). சார்புகளின் சேர்ப்பு பரிமாற்றுப் பண்பை நிறைவு செய்யாது, ஆனால் சேர்ப்புப் பண்பை நிறைவு செய்யும்.

CHAPTER 1 RELATIONS AND FUNCTIONS

ORDERED PAIRS AND CARTESIAN PRODUCT OF SETS (PAGE 17)

An ordered pair (a, b) consists of two elements specified in a definite strict order where a is the first coordinate and b is the second coordinate: (a, b) = (c, d) if and only if a = c and b = d. The Cartesian product A x B of two non-empty sets A and B is the set of all possible ordered pairs such that the first element belongs to A and the second belongs to B: A x B = {(a, b) : a in A, b in B}. If n(A) = p and n(B) = q, then the cardinal number n(A x B) = p * q. The Cartesian product is non-commutative: A x B != B x A in general, but n(A x B) = n(B x A). Cartesian product of three sets A x B x C forms ordered triplets (a, b, c) representing coordinates in three-dimensional geometric space.

CHAPTER 1 RELATIONS AND FUNCTIONS

RELATIONS: DOMAIN, CO-DOMAIN, RANGE, AND TYPES (PAGE 18)

Let A and B be two non-empty sets. A relation R from A to B is a formal mathematical subset of the Cartesian product A x B: R is a subset of A x B. If an ordered pair (a, b) belongs to R, we write a R b (a is related to b). 1. Domain of R = {x in A : (x, y) in R for some y in B}. 2. Co-domain of R is the entire destination set B. 3. Range of R = {y in B : (x, y) in R for some x in A}. The range is always a subset of the co-domain. A null relation contains no elements (R = empty set). Total possible relations from A to B equals 2^(p * q).

CHAPTER 1 RELATIONS AND FUNCTIONS

FUNCTIONS: DEFINITION, ARROW DIAGRAMS, AND VERTICAL LINE TEST (PAGE 19)

A function (or mapping) f from set A to set B (denoted f: A -> B) is a specialized relation wherein every element x in the domain set A is associated with one and only one unique element y in the co-domain set B: y = f(x). Every function is a relation, but not every relation is a function. Representation methods: 1. Set of ordered pairs. 2. Arrow diagram. 3. Table form. 4. Graphical representation. Vertical Line Test: A curve drawn in the XY-plane represents a function if and only if every vertical line intersects the curve at at most one point.

TYPES OF FUNCTIONS: ONE-TO-ONE, ONTO, BIJECTION, AND COMPOSITION (PAGE 28)

Classification of functions: 1. One-to-one function (Injective): distinct elements in domain A have distinct unique images in B (f(x1) = f(x2) implies x1 = x2). Tested via Horizontal Line Test. 2. Many-to-one function: two or more domain elements share the same image. 3. Onto function (Surjective): every element in co-domain B is the image of at least one element in domain A (Range = Co-domain). 4. Bijective function: both one-to-one and onto simultaneously; possesses a unique inverse function. Composition of functions: if f: A -> B and g: B -> C, then composite function (g o f)(x) = g(f(x)). Composition is non-commutative (f o g != g o f) but associative ((f o g) o h = f o (g o h)). Linear function f(x) = mx + c, quadratic f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c, cubic f(x) = ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d, and reciprocal function f(x) = 1/x.

CHAPTER 1 RELATIONS AND FUNCTIONS

ORDERED PAIRS AND CARTESIAN PRODUCT OF SETS (PAGE 29)

An ordered pair (a, b) consists of two elements specified in a definite strict order where a is the first coordinate and b is the second coordinate: (a, b) = (c, d) if and only if a = c and b = d. The Cartesian product A x B of two non-empty sets A and B is the set of all possible ordered pairs such that the first element belongs to A and the second belongs to B: A x B = {(a, b) : a in A, b in B}. If n(A) = p and n(B) = q, then the cardinal number n(A x B) = p * q. The Cartesian product is non-commutative: A x B != B x A in general, but n(A x B) = n(B x A). Cartesian product of three sets A x B x C forms ordered triplets (a, b, c) representing coordinates in three-dimensional geometric space.

CHAPTER 1 RELATIONS AND FUNCTIONS

RELATIONS: DOMAIN, CO-DOMAIN, RANGE, AND TYPES (PAGE 30)

Let A and B be two non-empty sets. A relation R from A to B is a formal mathematical subset of the Cartesian product A x B: R is a subset of A x B. If an ordered pair (a, b) belongs to R, we write a R b (a is related to b). 1. Domain of R = {x in A : (x, y) in R for some y in B}. 2. Co-domain of R is the entire destination set B. 3. Range of R = {y in B : (x, y) in R for some x in A}. The range is always a subset of the co-domain. A null relation contains no elements (R = empty set). Total possible relations from A to B equals 2^(p * q).

CHAPTER 1 RELATIONS AND FUNCTIONS

FUNCTIONS: DEFINITION, ARROW DIAGRAMS, AND VERTICAL LINE TEST (PAGE 31)

A function (or mapping) f from set A to set B (denoted f: A -> B) is a specialized relation wherein every element x in the domain set A is associated with one and only one unique element y in the co-domain set B: y = f(x). Every function is a relation, but not every relation is a function. Representation methods: 1. Set of ordered pairs. 2. Arrow diagram. 3. Table form. 4. Graphical representation. Vertical Line Test: A curve drawn in the XY-plane represents a function if and only if every vertical line intersects the curve at at most one point.

CHAPTER 2 NUMBERS AND SEQUENCES

EUCLID DIVISION LEMMA AND DIVISION ALGORITHM (PAGE 37)

Euclid Division Lemma states that for any two given positive integers a and b, there exist unique whole numbers q (quotient) and r (remainder) satisfying: a = b * q + r, where 0 <= r < b. When r = 0, b divides a completely. Euclid Division Algorithm is a systematic iterative technique applying this lemma to compute the Highest Common Factor (HCF / GCD) of two large numbers: divide larger a by b yielding remainder r1; if r1 != 0, divide b by r1 yielding r2, continuing iteratively until the remainder becomes exactly zero. The final non-zero divisor is the HCF: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, r).

text:
CHAPTER 2 NUMBERS AND SEQUENCES

FUNDAMENTAL THEOREM OF ARITHMETIC AND MODULAR ARITHMETIC (PAGE 38)

The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic states that every composite integer greater than 1 can be uniquely factorized as the product of prime numbers, up to the permutation of factors: N = p1^a1 * p2^a2 * ... * pk^ak. Modular arithmetic: for integers a, b and positive modulus n, we write a = b (mod n) (read: a is congruent to b modulo n) if and only if n divides the difference (a - b) completely without remainder. Properties: if a = b (mod n) and c = d (mod n), then (a + c) = (b + d) (mod n) and (a * c) = (b * d) (mod n). Used extensively in clock arithmetic, calendar day computations, and modern public-key cryptography algorithms.

text:
CHAPTER 2 NUMBERS AND SEQUENCES

ARITHMETIC PROGRESSION: GENERAL TERM AND SUM FORMULA (PAGE 39)

An Arithmetic Progression (AP) is a sequence of numbers in which each term is obtained by adding a fixed constant common difference d to the preceding term: a, a+d, a+2d, a+3d, ... Common difference d = t_n - t_(n-1). 1. The n-th general term is given by: t_n = a + (n - 1) * d. 2. Total number of terms in a finite AP with last term l is: n = ((l - a) / d) + 1. 3. Sum of the first n terms S_n is: S_n = (n / 2) * [2*a + (n - 1)*d] = (n / 2) * [a + l]. Three consecutive terms in an AP are represented symmetrically as: (a - d), a, (a + d) with common difference d. Four consecutive terms: (a - 3d), (a - d), (a + d), (a + 3d) with difference 2d.

Arithmetic Progression: General Term and Sum Formula (பக்கம் 39)

கூட்டுத் தொடர்வரிசை (AP): பொது வடிவம்: a, a+d, a+2d, ... n-வது உறுப்பு t_n = a + (n - 1) d. முதல் n உறுப்புகளின் கூடுதல் S_n = (n / 2) [2a + (n - 1) d] = (n / 2) [a + l]. கூட்டுத் தொடரில் உள்ள அடுத்தடுத்த மூன்று உறுப்புகள்: (a - d), a, (a + d).

chapter: Chapter 2 Numbers and Sequences
text:
CHAPTER 2 NUMBERS AND SEQUENCES

GEOMETRIC PROGRESSION AND SPECIAL SERIES SUMMATION (PAGE 40)

A Geometric Progression (GP) is a sequence where each term after the first is obtained by multiplying the previous term by a fixed non-zero common ratio r: a, a*r, a*r^2, a*r^3, ... Common ratio r = t_n / t_(n-1). 1. The n-th general term is: t_n = a * r^(n-1). 2. Sum of first n terms: S_n = a * (r^n - 1) / (r - 1) for r > 1, or S_n = a * (1 - r^n) / (1 - r) for r < 1. Sum to infinity of a decreasing GP (|r| < 1): S_inf = a / (1 - r). Special Series standard summation formulas: 1. Sum of first n natural numbers: Sigma k = n * (n + 1) / 2. 2. Sum of first n odd numbers: Sigma (2k - 1) = n^2. 3. Sum of squares of first n natural numbers: Sigma k^2 = n * (n + 1) * (2n + 1) / 6. 4. Sum of cubes of first n natural numbers: Sigma k^3 = [n * (n + 1) / 2]^2 = (Sigma k)^2.

EUCLID DIVISION LEMMA AND DIVISION ALGORITHM (PAGE 41)

Euclid Division Lemma states that for any two given positive integers a and b, there exist unique whole numbers q (quotient) and r (remainder) satisfying: a = b * q + r, where 0 <= r < b. When r = 0, b divides a completely. Euclid Division Algorithm is a systematic iterative technique applying this lemma to compute the Highest Common Factor (HCF / GCD) of two large numbers: divide larger a by b yielding remainder r1; if r1 != 0, divide b by r1 yielding r2, continuing iteratively until the remainder becomes exactly zero. FUNDAMENTAL THEOREM OF ARITHMETIC AND MODULAR ARITHMETIC (PAGE 42)

The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic states that every composite integer greater than 1 can be uniquely factorized as the product of prime numbers, up to the permutation of factors: N = p1^a1 * p2^a2 * ... * pk^ak. Properties: if a = b (mod n) and c = d (mod n), then (a + c) = (b + d) (mod n) and (a * c) = (b * d) (mod n). CHAPTER 2 NUMBERS AND SEQUENCES

ARITHMETIC PROGRESSION: GENERAL TERM AND SUM FORMULA (PAGE 43)

An Arithmetic Progression (AP) is a sequence of numbers in which each term is obtained by adding a fixed constant common difference d to the preceding term: a, a+d, a+2d, a+3d, ... Common difference d = t_n - t_(n-1). 1. The n-th general term is given by: t_n = a + (n - 1) * d. 2. Total number of terms in a finite AP with last term l is: n = ((l - a) / d) + 1. 3. Sum of the first n terms S_n is: S_n = (n / 2) * [2*a + (n - 1)*d] = (n / 2) * [a + l]. Three consecutive terms in an AP are represented symmetrically as: (a - d), a, (a + d) with common difference d. Four consecutive terms: (a - 3d), (a - d), (a + d), (a + 3d) with difference 2d.

A Geometric Progression (GP) is a sequence where each term after the first is obtained by multiplying the previous term by a fixed non-zero common ratio r: a, a*r, a*r^2, a*r^3, ... FUNDAMENTAL THEOREM OF ARITHMETIC AND MODULAR ARITHMETIC (PAGE 54)

The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic states that every composite integer greater than 1 can be uniquely factorized as the product of prime numbers, up to the permutation of factors: N = p1^a1 * p2^a2 * ... * pk^ak. CHAPTER 2 NUMBERS AND SEQUENCES

ARITHMETIC PROGRESSION: GENERAL TERM AND SUM FORMULA (PAGE 55)

An Arithmetic Progression (AP) is a sequence of numbers in which each term is obtained by adding a fixed constant common difference d to the preceding term: a, a+d, a+2d, a+3d, ... Common difference d = t_n - t_(n-1). 1. The n-th general term is given by: t_n = a + (n - 1) * d. 2. Total number of terms in a finite AP with last term l is: n = ((l - a) / d) + 1. 3. Sum of the first n terms S_n is: S_n = (n / 2) * [2*a + (n - 1)*d] = (n / 2) * [a + l]. Three consecutive terms in an AP are represented symmetrically as: (a - d), a, (a + d) with common difference d. Four consecutive terms: (a - 3d), (a - d), (a + d), (a + 3d) with difference 2d.

GEOMETRIC PROGRESSION AND SPECIAL SERIES SUMMATION (PAGE 56)

A Geometric Progression (GP) is a sequence where each term after the first is obtained by multiplying the previous term by a fixed non-zero common ratio r: a, a*r, a*r^2, a*r^3, ... Common ratio r = t_n / t_(n-1). 1. The n-th general term is: t_n = a * r^(n-1). 2. Sum of first n terms: S_n = a * (r^n - 1) / (r - 1) for r > 1, or S_n = a * (1 - r^n) / (1 - r) for r < 1. Sum to infinity of a decreasing GP (|r| < 1): S_inf = a / (1 - r). Special Series standard summation formulas: 1. Sum of first n natural numbers: Sigma k = n * (n + 1) / 2. 2. Sum of first n odd numbers: Sigma (2k - 1) = n^2. 3. Sum of squares of first n natural numbers: Sigma k^2 = n * (n + 1) * (2n + 1) / 6. 4. Sum of cubes of first n natural numbers: Sigma k^3 = [n * (n + 1) / 2]^2 = (Sigma k)^2.

EUCLID DIVISION LEMMA AND DIVISION ALGORITHM (PAGE 57)

Euclid Division Lemma states that for any two given positive integers a and b, there exist unique whole numbers q (quotient) and r (remainder) satisfying: a = b * q + r, where 0 <= r < b. When r = 0, b divides a completely. Euclid Division Algorithm is a systematic iterative technique applying this lemma to compute the Highest Common Factor (HCF / GCD) of two large numbers: divide larger a by b yielding remainder r1; if r1 != 0, divide b by r1 yielding r2, continuing iteratively until the remainder becomes exactly zero. The final non-zero divisor is the HCF: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, r).

CHAPTER 2 NUMBERS AND SEQUENCES

ARITHMETIC PROGRESSION: GENERAL TERM AND SUM FORMULA (PAGE 67)

An Arithmetic Progression (AP) is a sequence of numbers in which each term is obtained by adding a fixed constant common difference d to the preceding term: a, a+d, a+2d, a+3d, ... Common difference d = t_n - t_(n-1). 1. The n-th general term is given by: t_n = a + (n - 1) * d. 2. Total number of terms in a finite AP with last term l is: n = ((l - a) / d) + 1. 3. Sum of the first n terms S_n is: S_n = (n / 2) * [2*a + (n - 1)*d] = (n / 2) * [a + l]. Three consecutive terms in an AP are represented symmetrically as: (a - d), a, (a + d) with common difference d. Four consecutive terms: (a - 3d), (a - d), (a + d), (a + 3d) with difference 2d.

GEOMETRIC PROGRESSION AND SPECIAL SERIES SUMMATION (PAGE 68)

A Geometric Progression (GP) is a sequence where each term after the first is obtained by multiplying the previous term by a fixed non-zero common ratio r: a, a*r, a*r^2, a*r^3, ... Common ratio r = t_n / t_(n-1). 1. The n-th general term is: t_n = a * r^(n-1). 2. Sum of first n terms: S_n = a * (r^n - 1) / (r - 1) for r > 1, or S_n = a * (1 - r^n) / (1 - r) for r < 1. Sum to infinity of a decreasing GP (|r| < 1): S_inf = a / (1 - r). Special Series standard summation formulas: 1. Sum of first n natural numbers: Sigma k = n * (n + 1) / 2. 2. Sum of first n odd numbers: Sigma (2k - 1) = n^2. 3. Sum of squares of first n natural numbers: Sigma k^2 = n * (n + 1) * (2n + 1) / 6. 4. Sum of cubes of first n natural numbers: Sigma k^3 = [n * (n + 1) / 2]^2 = (Sigma k)^2.

CHAPTER 2 NUMBERS AND SEQUENCES

EUCLID DIVISION LEMMA AND DIVISION ALGORITHM (PAGE 69)

Euclid Division Lemma states that for any two given positive integers a and b, there exist unique whole numbers q (quotient) and r (remainder) satisfying: a = b * q + r, where 0 <= r < b. When r = 0, b divides a completely. Euclid Division Algorithm is a systematic iterative technique applying this lemma to compute the Highest Common Factor (HCF / GCD) of two large numbers: divide larger a by b yielding remainder r1; if r1 != 0, divide b by r1 yielding r2, continuing iteratively until the remainder becomes exactly zero. The final non-zero divisor is the HCF: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, r).

CHAPTER 2 NUMBERS AND SEQUENCES

FUNDAMENTAL THEOREM OF ARITHMETIC AND MODULAR ARITHMETIC (PAGE 70)

The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic states that every composite integer greater than 1 can be uniquely factorized as the product of prime numbers, up to the permutation of factors: N = p1^a1 * p2^a2 * ... * pk^ak. Modular arithmetic: for integers a, b and positive modulus n, we write a = b (mod n) (read: a is congruent to b modulo n) if and only if n divides the difference (a - b) completely without remainder. Properties: if a = b (mod n) and c = d (mod n), then (a + c) = (b + d) (mod n) and (a * c) = (b * d) (mod n). Used extensively in clock arithmetic, calendar day computations, and modern public-key cryptography algorithms.

CHAPTER 2 NUMBERS AND SEQUENCES

GEOMETRIC PROGRESSION AND SPECIAL SERIES SUMMATION (PAGE 80)

A Geometric Progression (GP) is a sequence where each term after the first is obtained by multiplying the previous term by a fixed non-zero common ratio r: a, a*r, a*r^2, a*r^3, ... Common ratio r = t_n / t_(n-1). 1. The n-th general term is: t_n = a * r^(n-1). 2. Sum of first n terms: S_n = a * (r^n - 1) / (r - 1) for r > 1, or S_n = a * (1 - r^n) / (1 - r) for r < 1. Sum to infinity of a decreasing GP (|r| < 1): S_inf = a / (1 - r). Special Series standard summation formulas: 1. Sum of first n natural numbers: Sigma k = n * (n + 1) / 2. 2. Sum of first n odd numbers: Sigma (2k - 1) = n^2. 3. Sum of squares of first n natural numbers: Sigma k^2 = n * (n + 1) * (2n + 1) / 6. 4. Sum of cubes of first n natural numbers: Sigma k^3 = [n * (n + 1) / 2]^2 = (Sigma k)^2.

CHAPTER 2 NUMBERS AND SEQUENCES

EUCLID DIVISION LEMMA AND DIVISION ALGORITHM (PAGE 81)

Euclid Division Lemma states that for any two given positive integers a and b, there exist unique whole numbers q (quotient) and r (remainder) satisfying: a = b * q + r, where 0 <= r < b. When r = 0, b divides a completely. Euclid Division Algorithm is a systematic iterative technique applying this lemma to compute the Highest Common Factor (HCF / GCD) of two large numbers: divide larger a by b yielding remainder r1; if r1 != 0, divide b by r1 yielding r2, continuing iteratively until the remainder becomes exactly zero. The final non-zero divisor is the HCF: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, r).

CHAPTER 2 NUMBERS AND SEQUENCES

FUNDAMENTAL THEOREM OF ARITHMETIC AND MODULAR ARITHMETIC (PAGE 82)

The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic states that every composite integer greater than 1 can be uniquely factorized as the product of prime numbers, up to the permutation of factors: N = p1^a1 * p2^a2 * ... * pk^ak. Modular arithmetic: for integers a, b and positive modulus n, we write a = b (mod n) (read: a is congruent to b modulo n) if and only if n divides the difference (a - b) completely without remainder. Properties: if a = b (mod n) and c = d (mod n), then (a + c) = (b + d) (mod n) and (a * c) = (b * d) (mod n). Used extensively in clock arithmetic, calendar day computations, and modern public-key cryptography algorithms.

CHAPTER 2 NUMBERS AND SEQUENCES

ARITHMETIC PROGRESSION: GENERAL TERM AND SUM FORMULA (PAGE 83)

An Arithmetic Progression (AP) is a sequence of numbers in which each term is obtained by adding a fixed constant common difference d to the preceding term: a, a+d, a+2d, a+3d, ... Common difference d = t_n - t_(n-1). 1. The n-th general term is given by: t_n = a + (n - 1) * d. 2. Total number of terms in a finite AP with last term l is: n = ((l - a) / d) + 1. 3. Sum of the first n terms S_n is: S_n = (n / 2) * [2*a + (n - 1)*d] = (n / 2) * [a + l]. Three consecutive terms in an AP are represented symmetrically as: (a - d), a, (a + d) with common difference d. Four consecutive terms: (a - 3d), (a - d), (a + d), (a + 3d) with difference 2d.

CHAPTER 3 ALGEBRA

SIMULTANEOUS LINEAR EQUATIONS IN THREE VARIABLES (PAGE 86)

A system of three linear equations in three variables x, y, z has the general algebraic form: a1*x + b1*y + c1*z = d1, a2*x + b2*y + c2*z = d2, a3*x + b3*y + c3*z = d3. Geometric interpretation: each linear equation represents a flat plane in 3D Euclidean space. Solving via method of elimination: eliminate one variable between two pairs to yield a 2x2 system, then solve for the second and back-substitute. Types of solutions: 1. Unique single solution (point of intersection): system is consistent and independent. 2. Infinitely many solutions (planes intersect along a common line or coincide): system is consistent and dependent (0 = 0). 3. No solution (planes parallel or intersect without common line): system is inconsistent (false equality like 0 = 5).

CHAPTER 3 ALGEBRA

GCD AND LCM OF POLYNOMIALS AND RATIONAL EXPRESSIONS (PAGE 87)

The Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) of polynomials is the highest common factor dividing each polynomial, computed via factorization or Euclidean long division algorithm: f(x) = g(x) * q(x) + r(x). The Least Common Multiple (LCM) is the polynomial of lowest degree containing each given polynomial as a factor. Fundamental relationship: f(x) * g(x) = GCD(f(x), g(x)) * LCM(f(x), g(x)). Rational algebraic expressions P(x) / Q(x) (where Q(x) != 0) are reduced to lowest terms by cancelling common polynomial factors. Excluded values are values of the variable making the denominator zero: Q(x) = 0.

CHAPTER 3 ALGEBRA

SQUARE ROOT OF POLYNOMIALS BY DIVISION METHOD (PAGE 88)

The square root of a polynomial of even degree 2n is a polynomial of degree n: sqrt(P(x)) = |Q(x)|. The long division method arranges terms in descending powers of the variable with zero coefficients for missing terms. In each step: 1. Find the square root of the first term to start the quotient. 2. Subtract its square and bring down the next pair of terms. 3. Double the current quotient to form the trial divisor. 4. Determine the next quotient term by dividing the leading remainder term by the doubled divisor leading term. The process continues until the final remainder is zero, yielding the square root.

QUADRATIC EQUATIONS: METHODS AND NATURE OF ROOTS (PAGE 89)

A quadratic equation in standard algebraic form is: a*x^2 + b*x + c = 0 (where a != 0). Solution methods: 1. Factorization by splitting the middle term. 2. Completing the square. 3. Quadratic formula: x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4*a*c)] / (2*a). The Discriminant is Delta = b^2 - 4*a*c. Nature of roots based on Delta: 1. If Delta > 0: roots are real and unequal. 2. If Delta = 0: roots are real and equal (x = -b / 2a). 3. If Delta < 0: roots are complex (no real roots). Relation between roots alpha, beta and coefficients: Sum of roots alpha + beta = -b / a; Product of roots alpha * beta = c / a. Quadratic equation formed from roots: x^2 - (alpha + beta)*x + (alpha * beta) = 0.

இருபடிச் சமன்பாடுகள் மற்றும் மூலங்களின் தன்மை: ax^2 + bx + c = 0. சூத்திரம்: x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)] / (2a). தன்மை காட்டி Delta = b^2 - 4ac: 1. Delta > 0 எனில் மெய் மற்றும் சமமற்ற மூலங்கள். 2. Delta = 0 எனில் மெய் மற்றும் சமமான மூலங்கள். 3. Delta < 0 எனில் மெய் மூலங்கள் இல்லை. மூலங்களின் கூடுதல் = -b/a, பெருக்கற்பலன் = c/a.

MATRICES: OPERATIONS AND TRANSPOSE (PAGE 90)

A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers or expressions arranged in m horizontal rows and n vertical columns, with order m x n. Types of matrices: row matrix (1 x n), column matrix (m x 1), square matrix (m = n), diagonal matrix (non-zero entries only on principal diagonal), scalar matrix, identity matrix I (diagonal entries 1, others 0), and zero/null matrix O. Operations: Addition/subtraction requires identical matrix dimensions. Scalar multiplication multiplies every entry by scalar k. Matrix multiplication: Product A * B is defined only if number of columns in A equals number of rows in B ((m x n) * (n x p) -> (m x p)). Matrix multiplication is associative (A(BC) = (AB)C) and distributive (A(B+C) = AB + AC), but non-commutative (AB != BA in general). Transpose of matrix A (denoted A^T) swaps rows into columns: (A^T)^T = A, (A + B)^T = A^T + B^T, and reversal law of transpose: (AB)^T = B^T * A^T.

SQUARE ROOT OF POLYNOMIALS BY DIVISION METHOD (PAGE 93)

The square root of a polynomial of even degree 2n is a polynomial of degree n: sqrt(P(x)) = |Q(x)|. The long division method arranges terms in descending powers of the variable with zero coefficients for missing terms. In each step: 1. Find the square root of the first term to start the quotient. 2. Subtract its square and bring down the next pair of terms. 3. Double the current quotient to form the trial divisor. 4. Determine the next quotient term by dividing the leading remainder term by the doubled divisor leading term. The process continues until the final remainder is zero, yielding the square root.

QUADRATIC EQUATIONS: METHODS AND NATURE OF ROOTS (PAGE 94)

A quadratic equation in standard algebraic form is: a*x^2 + b*x + c = 0 (where a != 0). Solution methods: 1. Factorization by splitting the middle term. 2. Completing the square. 3. Quadratic formula: x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4*a*c)] / (2*a). The Discriminant is Delta = b^2 - 4*a*c. Nature of roots based on Delta: 1. If Delta > 0: roots are real and unequal. 2. If Delta = 0: roots are real and equal (x = -b / 2a). 3. If Delta < 0: roots are complex (no real roots). Relation between roots alpha, beta and coefficients: Sum of roots alpha + beta = -b / a; Product of roots alpha * beta = c / a. Quadratic equation formed from roots: x^2 - (alpha + beta)*x + (alpha * beta) = 0.
